title: An array literal in an attribute's payload is an `array<mixed>`, so a typed array field cannot take one.
text: `type T = {list: array<int>};` and `#[T(list: [1, 2])]` is `E0401` ("expected `{list: array<int>}`, found `{list: array<mixed>}`"), and `array<string>` fails the same way. A field typed `array<mixed>` accepts the literal. The same literal at an `array<int>` local compiles, so the payload is checked without the shape's field type as the expected type. `rule:attributes/payload-is-a-compile-time-constant` allows an array literal of constants, and today it fits only an `array<mixed>` field. It closes when an array literal in a named attribute is checked against the field's declared array type, with a conformance case.
